provider.remediation: Pi subagent provider unavailable. Run `pi install npm:pi-subagents`, then restart Pi.

hooksDispatchModel: Pi loads src/extension.mjs once. At session_start the extension uses Pi's public pi.getAllTools() API and accepts any configured tool named exactly subagent, whether active or inactive. Generated child carriers register that transport at maxSubagentDepth 2, while Component-compiled canonical capabilities remain dispatch authority. Missing or malformed tool metadata leaves the session readable and blocks Write/Edit/Bash with the declared remediation. Parent terminal observers keep bounded nonblocking candidates until exact component/native correlation succeeds; only validated exact stop failures enter the mutation-blocking pending set.

session_start.behavior: probes configured generic subagent readiness through pi.getAllTools, then binds a root session or publishes a validated immediate Shepherd child start; failures leave mutation blocked

message_end.behavior: best-effort child-local stop only for Pi terminal assistant messages with stopReason stop and no tool call

agent_settled.behavior: retries child-local and parent-observed terminal work at a safe lifecycle boundary

tool_result.behavior: observes attached foreground subagent terminal results and closes each explicitly indexed validated child

subagent:foreground-complete.behavior: observes detached foreground completion without treating the earlier detached tool result as terminal

subagent:async-complete.behavior: observes explicitly indexed async child results; async-started is never stop authority

tool_call.behavior: before normal mutation guarding, blocks managed-child subagent calls when the already-resolved Component canonical capabilities omit dispatch; otherwise blocks on provider readiness or exact correlated stop failures, retries bounded nonblocking pre-correlation candidates, then resolves exact native identity and evaluates the component guard

session_shutdown.behavior: performs a final terminal retry and removes process and public-event listeners
